I can't write `tasks.md` directly because this request asked me not to use any tools. Here's the full file content, ready to paste in.

I haven't changed the plan. Where it left something open, I picked a default and marked it **[Assumed]** so the team can swap it quickly if the meeting decided otherwise.

```markdown
# User Data Export — Implementation Tasks

**Target:** Ship next week
**Plan:** API endpoint that exports all of a user's data; easiest format; fast.

## Assumed defaults (confirm or swap — not blocking)
- **Format:** JSON (single document, one top-level key per data domain). [Assumed]
- **Delivery:** Synchronous response for typical users; async job + download link if payload exceeds a size/time threshold. [Assumed]
- **Who can export:** Authenticated user exports *only their own* data. [Assumed]

---

## 1. Data inventory
- [ ] 1.1 List every table/store/service holding user-linked data (DB tables, blob storage, logs, third-party systems).
- [ ] 1.2 For each source, record: owner, user-key column, approx row volume per user.
- [ ] 1.3 Mark fields to exclude (password hashes, internal security tokens, other users' PII in shared records).
- [ ] 1.4 Get the inventory signed off by each data owner. Missing a source means the export is not "all" data.

## 2. API contract
- [ ] 2.1 Define endpoint: `GET /api/v1/users/me/export` (or `POST` to start a job if async).
- [ ] 2.2 Define JSON schema: `{ "exported_at", "user_id", "schema_version", "profile": {...}, "<domain>": [...] }`.
- [ ] 2.3 Define error responses (401, 403, 429, 500) and async job states (`pending`, `ready`, `failed`, `expired`).
- [ ] 2.4 Publish contract to frontend/consumers.

## 3. Auth & access control
- [ ] 3.1 Require authenticated session/token on the endpoint.
- [ ] 3.2 Enforce user can export only their own data (no `user_id` param accepted from the client; derive from auth context).
- [ ] 3.3 Decide whether admin/support export is in scope. If yes, separate permission + audit. [Assumed: out of scope]
- [ ] 3.4 Consider step-up auth (re-enter password / recent login) since this returns full PII.

## 4. Export implementation
- [ ] 4.1 Build one collector per data domain from the inventory (1.1), each returning serializable data.
- [ ] 4.2 Aggregator that runs collectors (in parallel where safe) and assembles the JSON document.
- [ ] 4.3 Stream the response rather than building it fully in memory.
- [ ] 4.4 Apply field exclusions from 1.3.
- [ ] 4.5 Include `schema_version` so the format can evolve.

## 5. Performance ("should be fast")
- [ ] 5.1 Define a target (e.g. p95 < N seconds for typical user) and the async threshold.
- [ ] 5.2 Ensure each collector query is indexed on the user key.
- [ ] 5.3 Run collectors against a read replica if available.
- [ ] 5.4 Implement async path for large users: background job → write to private storage → time-limited signed download URL.
- [ ] 5.5 Load test with a heavy synthetic user.

## 6. Abuse protection
- [ ] 6.1 Rate limit per user (e.g. N exports per 24h).
- [ ] 6.2 Signed download URLs expire (e.g. 24h) and are single-user scoped.
- [ ] 6.3 Delete generated export files after expiry.

## 7. Audit & observability
- [ ] 7.1 Audit log each export request (user, time, IP, success/failure). Don't log the payload.
- [ ] 7.2 Metrics: request count, latency, payload size, failures per collector.
- [ ] 7.3 Alerting on elevated failure rate.

## 8. Testing
- [ ] 8.1 Unit tests per collector.
- [ ] 8.2 Integration test: export contains data from every inventoried source.
- [ ] 8.3 Authorization tests: user A cannot obtain user B's export (including via job IDs / download URLs).
- [ ] 8.4 Test excluded fields never appear in output.
- [ ] 8.5 Test empty/new user and very large user.

## 9. Release
- [ ] 9.1 Feature flag the endpoint.
- [ ] 9.2 Short API docs / user-facing help text.
- [ ] 9.3 Internal rollout → staged rollout → GA.
- [ ] 9.4 Rollback plan (flag off).

---

## Suggested schedule (one week)
| Day | Work |
|-----|------|
| Mon | 1 (inventory), 2 (contract), 3.1–3.2 |
| Tue–Wed | 4 (collectors + aggregator), 6.1 |
| Thu | 5 (perf + async path), 6.2–6.3, 7 |
| Fri | 8 (testing), 9 (flag + rollout) |

**Critical path:** Task 1.1 (data inventory). Everything else depends on knowing every source.
```

Two items deserve a quick check against the meeting notes, since getting them wrong would be costly after launch:

- **3.2:** users must be limited to exporting only their own data.
- **1.1:** the data inventory must actually be complete.

If the meeting chose a different format or delivery model, change the "Assumed defaults" block and tasks 4–5. The rest of the breakdown still applies.
